model.description: See the candidates running for mayor, councillor and school trustee in the 2026 General Local Election.

content.text: In October 2026, District residents will vote for and elect a mayor, six councillors, and four school trustees in the 2026 General Local Election.

Each candidate profile includes nomination and financial disclosure documents. All candidates are given the option submit a 250-word statement and photo. These profiles are provided as submitted and have not been edited by the District of North Vancouver.
The views expressed are those of the candidates and do not represent the District of North Vancouver.

content.text: Practical Leadership, Strong North Vancouver, United Canada Canada faces economic uncertainty, including tariff pressure and trade disputes with the United States. In difficult times, we must stand united as Canadians: supporting local businesses, protecting household budgets, and treating every tax dollar with care.

I have lived in North Vancouver for 38 years. I built my career here, raised my family here, and care deeply about this community. I am running for Mayor of the District of North Vancouver as an independent—with no slate and no party—because residents deserve a government that listens, explains how public money is spent, and takes responsibility when projects go off track. The North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant is one example. Metro Vancouver’s estimate rose from about $700 million in 2013 to $3.86 billion in 2024. The plant is necessary, but residents deserve public reporting, independent oversight, and a fair allocation of costs. I will advocate for all three wherever the District has a seat at the table.

My priorities are practical: predictable property taxes; housing for families, workers, and seniors that is supported by infrastructure while protecting neighbourhood character and green space; better coordination of road work and a united North Shore voice on transit; responsive municipal services; and stronger wildfire and emergency preparedness.

I bring an MBA in Global Management, a BSc in Computer Science, experience in business and operations, government and regulatory work, and service on three strata councils. Max Zahedi, max@maxformayor.ca

GRAHAM ALEXANDER FOR MAYOR: THE BUILDER VS. THE CAREER POLITICIAN Incumbent Mike Little has failed DNV taxpayers with runaway spending and taxes through the roof. North Vancouver urgently needs proven engineering expertise and leadership rather than political stagnation. As a UBC Electrical Engineering graduate, successful real estate developer at GGIQ Developments, and tech entrepreneur who founded StayRunners, Graham Alexander brings world-class systems-thinking to municipal leadership. He is fully dedicated to stopping financial waste and protecting taxpayers.

FOCUSED VISION TO WIN BY A LANDSLIDE: Stop Tax Waste: Execute an immediate forensic audit of the staggering $3.86B North Shore Wastewater Plant budget disaster. Move DNV: Fix bridge and arterial gridlock utilizing modern traffic synchronization and federal USNA framework backing. Build Smarter: Deploy AI-powered instant building permits to slash municipal review delays from months to minutes. "North Vancouver does not need career politicians making empty promises; it needs an engineer who builds functional systems. Together, we will rescue our district, audit the waste, and build a smarter, thriving community."

JOIN THE BUILDER'S GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT: Real civic progress starts with active community engagement and principled leadership. Get involved today, host a meet & greet, volunteer, and help build a transparent, accountable city hall that serves every resident.Official Website: www.grahamalexander.ca | Email: mayordnvga@gmail.com

I am Stephan Nieweler ("Dr. Transit") - running to be your next mayor! Born & raised in Upper Delbrook, I attended Handsworth & Capilano University, where I played on the men's basketball team. I completed a Master of Planning (Toronto) & related PhD (SFU).

My professional career has focused on delivering sustainable transport solutions. I worked on the Canada Line (on-budget, 110 days early!), the London Olympic transport plan & Mumbai's rail transit plan. I liaised with leading engineers & planners, gaining expertise implementing major infrastructure projects (lived in ON, Europe, Asia for a decade).
I returned to work at TransLink, teach (SFU) & conduct research (2018-20) justifying North Shore rail transit.

I have a plan to unlock traffic gridlock: (1) a new bridge next to Ironworkers with rail transit, dedicated HOV & cycling lanes; (2) new highway lanes for HOV from the bridge to Taylor Way, facilitating a new Horseshoe Bay to Phibbs express bus; (3) rail transit from Ambleside to Metrotown (SkyTrain) & along Hastings to downtown.

I’m committed to responsible development in designated growth areas, without sacrificing the character of mountainside neighbourhoods. Our walkable transit-oriented centres must reflect North Van through design & public art, offering the shops, services & (affordable) housing we need.

I want a healthy, active & connected North Van. I owned & operated a jazz club & am passionate that all residents have a chance to participate in sports, recreation & the arts. To succeed, we must build partnerships & invest in trails, parks, programs & space.
Dan Anderson is running for District Council because our community deserves responsible growth, accountable government, and infrastructure that keeps pace with development.

A lifelong North Shore resident, Dan lives in Seylynn with his beloved Labrador retriever, Nietzsche. He holds graduate degrees in Developmental Psychology and Education and is the co-founder of the Thinking Playground, a summer camp that helps children and youth develop critical-thinking skills.

For the past four years, he has served on the North Vancouver School Board, where he chaired the Audit Committee and helped rebuild the Board’s strategic reserves. Dan also serves as the spokesperson for the North Shore Neighbourhoods Alliance, a coalition of seven community associations seeking an independent, public inquiry into the Wastewater Treatment Plant project. This experience has strengthened his commitment to transparency, sound financial oversight, and ensuring regional bodies remain accountable to the communities they serve.

As a councillor, Dan will work to ensure infrastructure and public facilities keep pace with growth, address transportation gridlock, and protect taxpayers amid rising budgetary pressures. He will advocate for a fair renegotiation of household levies connected to the Wastewater project, meaningful local control over density and zoning, attainable housing for young families, and decisions that protect the balance among people, nature, and community.
Dan is asking voters to join him in restoring local control and building a more liveable, fiscally responsible District of North Van

Born and raised in North Vancouver, Jim Hanson is seeking his fourth term on District Council. Jim is married to Ruth Hanson, and together they have two adult children. Jim lives in Blueridge (20+ years) and is a practicing lawyer in North Vancouver.

If re-elected, Jim will commit to relentlessly pursuing transportation initiatives to relieve congestion, such as his idea to pave a third lane on the Cut eastbound between Lynn Valley Road and Mountain Highway, to separate North Vancouver residents from highway/bridge traffic. He will support investments in transit and active transportation. On housing, Jim will support development that addresses the needs of District residents (social, supportive, seniors and rental housing near transit hubs) and will not vote for large, expensive, strata development. Jim commits to only voting for tax increases that are at or below inflation. Jim will speak out loudly for accountability from Metro Vancouver for the North Shore Waste Water Treatment plant debacle and advocate for governance reform at Metro.

Jim has served on a variety of boards and committees, including the Policing Committee, Library Board, Heritage Committee, and the Advisory Committee on Disability Issues. Jim chairs the North Shore Standing Committee on Substance Use.

I grew up on the North Shore, and now I’m raising my family here. I’m running for District Council because I’ve watched people I know leave. They love it here. They want to stay. But increasingly, the math doesn’t work. Their kids can’t afford to stay, their parents can’t find somewhere smaller nearby, and the math doesn’t work. This election comes down to one question: Can people stay here? I believe we can make room for the future without taking away what people value about the North Shore. My approach is practical: protect what works, fix what does not, and plan ahead.

HOUSING: Homes for every stage of life, in the right places and close to transit, shops and services. The province has set the rules. We can spend years fighting them, or focus on getting the infrastructure and planning right for North Vancouver.

GETTING AROUND: We live between the mountains, rivers and the sea, with only so many ways to get around. Gridlock will continue unless people have reliable alternatives. I’ll push for true bus rapid transit on the R2, extend the Spirit Trail where it is feasible, and advocate for the Ironworkers crossing before congestion gets even worse.

ACCOUNTABILITY: We’re nearly 90,000 people, growing toward 100,000. If a decision can be made in public, it should be. I’ll push for regular release of closed-meeting items, easier public participation and a public dashboard showing what we’re building and what it costs. We can't ignore the fact that the region is growing. We can shape that growth, or let it shape us.
You can read more about my platform at aidankyle.ca
I know a brighter future is possible. I know we can lift those who need a hand, grow in harmony with each other and with the land, and build a more resilient future together.

I’ve worked in the mental health and substance use sector for 17 years. I see first-hand how systems can change lives. When people have stable housing, food in the fridge, and neighbours that care, they also have hope. What does a brighter future look like?
Truly affordable housing. We’re relying on for-profit systems to solve problems created by profits. Governments have an obligation to collaborate and build non-profit and co-op housing.

Building renters into the conversation. The number of renters in the District is growing, and many people (like me!) see renting as a long-term option rather than a temporary stopover. Renters need an advocate and they need to be part of decision-making.

Fast and reliable public transportation. We can’t simply pave our way out of traffic congestion. Expanding the transit network with RapidBus and Bus Rapid Transit creates real alternatives to driving. I don’t own a car and primarily use transit to get around, so I know just how many neighbourhoods aren’t served well.
Spaces for connection. Improving access to libraries, parks, recreation, sports, and cultural opportunities for everyone.
Climate justice. Protecting our land, air, and water from a perspective of equity.
I’m proud to be endorsed by the Vancouver and District Labour Council and CUPE 389. I’m a union member and I continue to support the workers that keep our communities running.

I am a 61 year resident of the District of North Vancouver, my family first settled here in the 1930’s in Deep Cove. My father and grandfather were small business owners. I am a single mother of 3 young adults, and 2 pups!

I am the longest serving Municipal Councillor on the North Shore, being elected consistently since 1996, serving 30 years in October! I believe the community returns me because I advocate first for the taxpayer, the community and the many businesses that have helped build this place. I am a huge believer in the power of community and the people who live here. I also believe I am returned to Council because people trust me. I am straightforward, honest, and have been consistent over those 30 years with my position on issues that face the District!
I remain committed to responsible spending, protecting the environment, prioritizing transportation infrastructure, supporting small business, and reviewing our Official Community Plan.

For the past 25 years, I have been proud to call the District of North Vancouver home. As a mother of two young adults, I am deeply grateful that our family has had the opportunity to live, grow, and build lasting connections here on the North Shore.

For the past eight years, I have had the privilege of serving as an elected North Vancouver School Board Trustee. In this role, I have advocated for students & families while working collaboratively with school district staff, the Ministry of Education, families, partner organizations, and our broader community. Community service has been an important part of my life for more than two decades. Over the years, I have been honored to serve on the boards of NVDPL, NS Disability Resource Centre, NV Band & Strings Parent Association, NS Safety Council & Presentation House Theatre. I have also volunteered with and participated in committees & initiatives involving the NS Women’s Centre, NS Family Services, NS Restorative Justice Society, MONOVA, Impact NS, Kelty Mental Health, NS Table Matters and Cops for Cancer. These experiences—as a trustee, volunteer, parent, and resident—have given me the opportunity to listen to people from across our community, understand different perspectives, build relationships, and work collaboratively toward practical solutions. They have also reinforced my belief that our community is strongest when we work together.
Every voice deserves to be heard. I believe in accountability, strong leadership, collaboration, and responsible decision-making that puts the best interests of District residents first.
A District for all to thrive for generations to come. That vision has inspired my public service since I was first elected in 2014.

Our neighbours, friends and families should be able to build roots, stay connected and see their future here at every stage of life. The next Council will make tough decisions about affordability and quality of life that will shape our community for generations. We must maintain and improve infrastructure, transportation and the services people rely on, while understanding long-term costs and demanding accountability for major projects.

Council is strongest when members each bring their different experience to the table and test decisions from more than one perspective. I bring the experience of serving two terms on District Council, a record of community volunteering and nonprofit leadership, and more than 15 years as a professional engineer working on major transportation infrastructure. I understand how local government works, where partnerships are needed and how Council decisions shape our community.

I also know what it means to choose North Vancouver, work to find a suitable home, raise my two children here and manage the everyday cost of living in this community. Together, these experiences help me bring people together, work through complex problems and keep Council decisions grounded in how they affect daily life.
I am running again to help Council make responsible decisions, protect what we value about North Vancouver and keep building a community where we can all make a good life.
North Vancouver has always been home. I am a lifelong resident of the District and have been proud to serve on Council since 2018. I live in Lynn Valley with my wife, Signy, and our two young kids.

Professionally, I have spent more than 20 years working in advertising and sales and hold a Bachelor of Music from UBC. During my time on Council, I have also served on a number of community boards and committees, including the Library Board, Museum and Archives Commission, and the District’s Climate Action Advisory Committee. I am running as an independent candidate and will continue to approach each issue on its merits, listen carefully to residents and work collaboratively to find practical solutions.

If re-elected, my priorities include improving how we move around the North Shore through better transit, safer walking and cycling connections, and strong advocacy for replacement of the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge. I will continue supporting thoughtful housing choices that help young people, families and seniors remain in our community, with most growth focused near town centres, transit, shops and services. I also want to advance financially responsible plans to renew aging community facilities, protect our parks, trails and natural environment, prepare for climate risks, and continue pushing for transparency and accountability at Metro Vancouver.
My goal is a connected, sustainable and welcoming North Vancouver where people of every generation can build a life and feel heard.

Thank you for taking the time to read my short bio. I am a passionate community member who is deeply grateful to call Lynn Creek home. My family and I chose North Vancouver because we found a place where we can put down roots for generations to come.

My professional and volunteer experiences have taken me across different fields, including project management, technology and education, as well as local and international community service. I have served on the Social Planning Advisory Council (SPAC) with the City Council, where I helped advise on grants supporting non-profit organizations and community initiatives. I have also organized shoreline cleanups and electronic recycling campaigns and volunteered with families navigating times of transition.

I’m running for District Councillor because I believe North Vancouver is changing, and I want to help us prepare thoughtfully for what comes next while preserving what makes this community special. I care about housing that allows people to put down roots, transportation that works for everyday life, strong neighbourhood connections, responsible growth, environmental stewardship, and preparing our community for climate and technological change.

I believe progress and preservation don’t have to be opposites. Good local government means listening with curiosity, asking thoughtful questions, working with others and planning proactively—not reactively. I want to help build a North Vancouver where communities can thrive and where future generations have the freedom to choose to call it home.

Catherine Pope is a District of North Vancouver Councillor and former investigative journalist who has spent her career asking tough questions on behalf of the public. Born and raised on the North Shore, Catherine came home after a career that took her across Canada and the UK.
Two decades as an investigative journalist with Global TV taught her to follow the facts and hold decision-makers to account. She brings the same approach to Council.

Catherine led the call for a public inquiry into the massive cost overruns at the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant. Council unanimously endorsed her motion, making the District the first municipality in Metro Vancouver to back an inquiry. She continues to fight for lower utility costs for NS taxpayers and change at Metro Van.

Since her election in 2022, Catherine has helped deliver more affordable housing, a new toddler playground, new pickleball courts and expanded recreation, safer streets, youth-centre funding and greater transparency in Council decision-making.

To tackle traffic congestion, she's pushing for a new bridge, SkyTrain, more transit and active transportation routes. Above all, she's working to keep the North Shore affordable for seniors, families, young people and workers.

Catherine served 20 years on the Victoria Foundation's Adoption and Permanency Committee and was on the board of the Disability Foundation. She champions youth mental health services and volunteered with school PACs and the NS homeless count.
Away from Council, she's a mom, pickleball player, e-bike rider, pet lover.
My vision: For DNV to be where people of all generations find community connections, opportunities for economic development & a place to thrive.

HOUSING: Explore alternative housing options (Co-op, rent to own, repurposed buildings, home sharing for seniors & students, and purpose-built homes for public sector workers) – to better meet the needs of local people
ECONOMY: Prioritize maintaining & growing commercial space so local residents can live and work here
TRANSPORTATION: Urge changes to combat traffic gridlock & encourage active transportation
COMMUNITY: Support additional childcare facilities so more families can find care close to home
CLIMATE: Add wildfire mitigation measures to DNV climate emergency actions

My Experience: Born and raised in Capilano-Highlands, and today my family lives in Lynn Valley. The District of North Vancouver is my home, my community & my people. I am a two-term elected school trustee, a role that involves responsible decision-making on policy, supporting families and educators, and championing student centred initiatives. I bring over 20 years of career experience in communications, public affairs, & community engagement. I have built my career on strengthening relationships, solving complex challenges, and ensuring people feel heard. With degrees in Urban Geography and Political Science from Queen’s University, I understand community development & good government, and I want to be part of delivering that for you.

I grew up on the North Shore and raised my family in the Seymour area, where I still live today. As a renter who commutes daily by transit across the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge, I understand firsthand the challenges many residents face, including traffic congestion, the impacts of growth and development, and the shortage of attainable housing. These are complex challenges that won’t be solved by one person or one council alone. They require collaboration among residents, businesses and all levels of government, and the decisions we make today will shape our community for generations. That perspective shapes my approach.

With more than 30 years of experience in both the public and private sectors, I have developed a proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships across all sectors of the community. I am particularly passionate about addressing affordable housing, homelessness, traffic congestion, and ensuring that the pace of development reflects the needs and priorities of the residents who live here. I care deeply about this community and don’t take for granted how fortunate we are to live here. Preserving what we value takes commitment.

My approach is simple: work together, build on our achievements, and remain open to learning from one another. That’s how we move our community forward. If elected, I will work tirelessly on your behalf. I encourage everyone to vote on October 17 and to choose candidates who understand and share your concerns.

My name is Mike Boehm and I am honored to be a candidate as a School Trustee in North Vancouver School District. I have been a North Vancouver District resident for close to 40 years and all four of our children were students with the School District in Elementary, French Immersion and High Schools.

I have been actively involved in a number of organizations related to children including President of Highlands Little League, North Shore Girls Softball, Director of Canuck Place; previous Chair of North Vancouver Chamber of Commerce as well as Not For Profit organizations including Chair of North Shore Community Foundation and a current director of The Hollyburn Society.

Over the years I have also coached various youth sports teams including baseball, softball, hockey and football. In May 2024 I was presented a District of North Vancouver Community Service token of appreciation.

I am a firm believer of listening, open communication and collaboration and believe my skillset and experience developed over the years would be an asset to the School District at all levels namely administration, teachers and support staff, students and parents.

I have long maintained in "giving back to the community to make our community better tomorrow than it was yesterday" and on Saturday October 17 I hope to receive your support. In my professional career, I was most recently Vice President, Business Development with KPMG

For the past eight years, it has been my honour to serve as Chair of the North Vancouver School District Parent Advisory Council (NVPAC/DPAC). During that time, I have engaged, collaborated, and worked alongside students, families and staff, gaining a deeper understanding of the opportunities and challenges within our school district. Students, families and staff deserve to know their voices matter, to feel heard and respected, and to be supported as essential partners in both our school communities and within the broader public education sector.

My professional experience in operations and governance has taught me that good decisions begin with listening. I understand the important distinction between governance and operations. Good governance means asking thoughtful questions, considering different perspectives, making informed decisions and ensuring public resources are used responsibly. It also means building trust through transparency, respect and accountability.

In 2024, I was honoured to receive the George Matthews Award for Excellence in Parent Leadership from the British Columbia Confederation of Parent Advisory Councils (BCCPAC), recognizing my commitment to supporting students and families across the North Vancouver School District. I care deeply about our North Vancouver schools and the people who make them such an important and special part of our community. I will listen with intention, work collaboratively, and lead with integrity. I would be deeply grateful for the opportunity to continue serving our schools and contributing to the community we share.

I am a professional actor, theatre arts instructor and a non-BCTF member of the Association of BC Drama Educators. My 40-year career has included teaching students age 3 to adult, developing curriculum, and helping connect families with arts education opportunities. Through my work as Performing Arts Education Coordinator at Evergreen Arts (Coquitlam 2014- 2018), I’ve seen how creative learning can build confidence, communication skills, and a sense of belonging. Strong public schools, engage families, and supportive, inclusive, secular learning environments are important for student success. I have also taught Mad Science; educational, interactive, science-based STEM programs.  I am an advocate for arts education, the arts IN education and the importance of the A in STEAM.

For the past 5 years I have also been working as a Constituency Advisor in MLA Susie Chant’s community office. I have knowledge of provincial government operations and the powers of the Ministry of Education. I believe this job involves listening to concerns, knowing who or where to direct those concerns and using relationships to effect change.

I understand the board’s fiduciary responsibility which includes ensuring any child in the district has access to a quality education, liaising with community organizations and social services to provide non-educational supports for kids, maintaining facilities and passing a balanced annual budget.

Go to https://michaelcharrois.wordpress.com/instructor/ for more information about my teaching. Go to https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-charrois-a9b50337/ and https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0153511/ for more information about my professional credits.
Fun fact: I played the role of Wiggens in 1992’s Academy Award-winning film Unforgiven.
Public education continues to evolve as we better understand the students we are educating, how they learn and what they need to thrive.

Having served as a School Trustee for four terms, I have seen that evolution firsthand. I am seeking re-election because I believe that experience and perspective are valuable as we continue to learn, adapt and improve. Throughout my time on the Board, I have worked to keep students at the centre of decision-making. I am known for listening and bringing concerns forward, even when I may not personally agree.

Good governance requires asking questions, considering different perspectives, being transparent and accountable, and being willing to learn and change. My priorities are Students First; Ethical, Transparent and Accountable Governance; Building Relationships Through Trust and Engagement; and Belonging, Opportunity and Well-Being. I will continue to advocate for strong literacy and numeracy, inclusive learning environments, and the resources needed to meet the needs of students in today’s classrooms. Every student should have opportunities to learn, participate, belong and reach their potential.

Public education is the backbone of a strong community. I want to continue bringing my experience, curiosity and willingness to listen to the Board, while building the relationships needed to support students today and into the future.

I have spent more than 23 years in public education, seeing firsthand the difference a great teacher and a strong school can make in the lives of students, families, and communities. I have worked as a secondary teacher, special education teacher, IB educator, and Vice Principal. I've taught in Ontario, Hong Kong, and British Columbia, giving me a broad perspective on education and the needs of students and school communities.

Throughout my career, I have supported students with diverse learning needs, worked to uphold high educational standards, and collaborated with families, educators, and support staff to build strong school communities. These experiences have given me a deep appreciation for the challenges and opportunities facing public education today.

I believe strong school leadership begins with listening, collaboration, and a clear focus on student success. I am committed to advocating for students, supporting educators and staff, and strengthening public education in North Vancouver. I am running because every student deserves the support and opportunity to succeed. I have seen classrooms become more complex, demands on teachers and educational assistants increase, and funding pressures place greater strain on schools. I believe we need to strengthen support without lowering expectations.

As a Trustee, I will bring my experience as an educator and school leader to advocate for students, support strong public schools, and help ensure the resources students and educators need reach our classrooms.

As a mother of two children in our public schools, I care deeply about the education our students experience today and the world we are preparing them for tomorrow.​Lynn Valley and North Vancouver are our home. Over the past decade, I have grown deep roots here volunteering in our schools, serving on non-profit boards, and bringing financial literacy directly into elementary classrooms.

With over 20 years of global leadership experience in finance, strategy, and governance, the focus remains on translating public resources into measurable, real-world impact inside every classroom. Strong governance is about delivering fiscal responsibility that puts classrooms first, championing future-focused education that prepares youth for life beyond graduation, and cultivating a school culture where every student feels a deep sense of belonging and every educator is supported.

My candidacy is not about seeking a position. Running for School Trustee is rooted in a single priority: putting students first and translating district resources into classroom excellence. Every child deserves an education that equips them with the confidence, resilience, and practical life skills to thrive: empowering them not simply to navigate the world around them, but to shape it.
Entering this election with warmth, humility, and a readiness to listen, learn, and serve. It would be an honour to earn your support and serve our North Vancouver community as School Board Trustee.
I believe the school system is key to a strong community foundation and I want to help ensure ours is exceptional.

Operational Expertise: My professional background is in finance, operations, and organizational efficiency. I have an eagle eye for unnecessary bottlenecks, and genuinely enjoy the process of untangling inefficiencies to improve processes and thoughtfully allocate resources.

Personally Invested: With 4 young children in (or about to enter) the North Van public school system, I am personally committed to ensuring our schools provide excellent educational experiences in the long-term. I also have an up-close understanding of the realities families experience as they navigate the system.

Community Experience: I have served on non-profit boards supporting children and volunteered with several community-based organizations on the north shore. I know what it looks like to work collaboratively, balance competing priorities, allocate limited resources, and make decisions in the best interests of the broader community.

High Quality Education I want to help reduce the burden of inefficient processes and unnecessary administration so teachers and staff can maximize the time and energy they spend providing high quality educational experiences for our children. I was lucky to grow up in North Van and attend school in the district. School fairs, sports days, and family dances created happy memories as well as a strong sense of community. I want to give back by contributing to a strong, effective, and forward-looking public school system for the next generation.
It has been an honour serving as a School Trustee with the North Vancouver Board of Education since 2018, including as Vice-Chair and Board Chair.

Over the past eight years, I have worked with students, families, educators, staff, and community partners to support student success, strengthen public education, and advance equitable learning opportunities. I am seeking re-election because I believe in the value of public education and the role our schools play in helping every student reach their full potential. While we have made meaningful progress, important work remains.

My priorities are student and staff well-being, inclusive learning, support for diverse learners, Truth and Reconciliation, responsible use of technology and innovation, fiscal responsibility, sustainability, and effective governance. I am Interim Associate University Librarian, Collections, at the University of British Columbia and an Honorary Lecturer at the Allard School of Law. My experience in higher education and public-sector leadership has reinforced the importance of sound governance, and stewardship of public resources. It has also strengthened my appreciation for the role public education plays in student success.

North Vancouver has much to be proud of in its public education system, and I look forward to building on that success. I remain committed to bringing people together and supporting the well-being and growth of every student. I would be honoured to continue serving North Vancouver.
To learn more about my background, experience, and my priorities, please visit www.georgetsiakos.ca

General local elections in B.C. are held every four years on the third Saturday in October.  General local elections (and by-elections) are the most direct way for the public to influence their local government, school district or other local governance body.
This page features the official results for the 2022, 2018, 2014, 2011, 2008, and 2005 local general elections, and the 2021 by-election.
These are the total numbers of voters and voting percentages for each District election dating back to 1996.
